prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Liberal Democrats Manifesto 1997 – Summary

Core purpose
Build and safeguard a fair, free and open society that balances liberty, equality and community; spreads power, wealth and opportunity; rejects centralised conformity; and uses active, democratic government to enable self-reliant people in strong communities. Markets drive prosperity, but government must invest, protect rights, tackle inequality and defend the environment. Policies are costed and accountable.

Education first
- Invest £2bn a year funded by 1p on the basic income tax rate.
- Universal high‑quality early years for all 3–4 year‑olds; double school books/equipment in year one; cut primary classes to max 30 within five years; £500m over five years for repairs; fully fund Special Educational Needs.
- Raise standards: General Teaching Council; stronger inspection of schools and LEAs; discipline and anti‑bullying; meaningful reporting; replace National Curriculum with a flexible Minimum Curriculum Entitlement; literacy drive.
- Life‑long learning: Individual Learning Accounts; replace student loans with income‑linked repayment; oppose top‑up fees; credit‑based system; workplace training via a 2% remissible levy (small firms exempt).

Stable, enterprising, greener economy
- Lock in stability: independent UK Reserve Bank (BoE) targeting low inflation; keep to a “golden rule” on borrowing; capital/current split; public‑private partnerships.
- Europe: support single currency only if Maastricht criteria are met, the UK qualifies and the public agrees in a referendum.
- Back small business: tackle late payment; cut red tape; fairer local business rating; seed capital; regional development agencies; shift R&D from military to civil; empower consumers and competition authorities; reform utility regulation and promote mutual models.
- Tax shift: reduce taxes on jobs/production; increase taxes on pollution/resource depletion; new indicators of quality of life.

Environment and transport
- Mainstream environmental goals; cut CO2 by 30% from 1990 levels in 15 years.
- Treble rail freight and double passengers by 2010; empower councils on road pricing to fund clean public transport; retain London Underground in public ownership with private finance for investment.
- Encourage fuel‑efficient cars: cut annual car tax to £10 for ≤1600cc, funded by gradual fuel duty rises; reform company car tax.
- National home insulation to end fuel poverty; phased carbon tax with offsetting cuts to VAT and employers’ NICs; boost renewables; no new nuclear subsidies; focus on safe waste management.
- Stronger countryside, wildlife and water protection; animal welfare reforms.

Safer, housed communities
- 3,000 more police on the beat; restorative justice; faster, fairer courts; targeted crime prevention; robust action on drugs; stronger victims’ rights; accountable policing.
- Housing: unlock council capital receipts; public‑private‑housing association partnerships; new Mortgage Benefit (protecting existing MIRAS); end rough sleeping by 2000; bring empty homes into use; fairer private renting; tackle homelessness.

NHS and care
- Extra £540m annually: recruit front‑line staff (e.g., 10,000 nurses or 5,000 doctors); six‑month moratorium on finance‑driven closures with independent audit; cut waits to max six months in three years.
- End two‑tier GP funding; national inspectorate; shift from bureaucracy to care; restore free eye and dental checks; prioritise prevention; independent Food Commission.
- Community care: greater choice and standards; Carer’s Benefit; fairer charging; raise care cost thresholds over time.

Clean, modern politics
- Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law), Human Rights Commission, Ministry of Justice; Freedom of Information Act; curb quangos; referendums on constitutional change.
- Proportional representation for all elections; reduce MPs by one‑third; democratic second chamber; fixed four‑year terms; clean party funding.
- Devolution: Scottish Parliament and Welsh Senedd with tax‑varying powers; elected English regional assemblies where wanted; stronger, better‑funded local government and local taxation reform.

Opportunity and fairness
- Break poverty traps: raise tax thresholds; simplify benefits into a Low Income Benefit; voluntary Citizens Service; regionally varied minimum wage; crack down on fraud and evasion.
- Older people: earnings‑linked top‑up; flexible retirement 60–70; anti‑age discrimination; expand funded personal/occupational pensions, with security and portability.
- Equal rights and anti‑discrimination for women, disabled people, ethnic minorities, and LGBT people; repeal Section 28; single age of consent.

International leadership
- Positive, democratic EU reform; enlargement; CAP/CFP reform (regional fisheries management).
- Defence through NATO; retain Trident at reduced warhead levels; pursue multilateral disarmament.
- Strengthen UN peacekeeping; back an International Criminal Court; lead on global environmental agreements; increase aid towards 0.7% GNP in 10 years; untie aid; human rights conditionality.
- Tighten arms export controls; ban landmines; promote fair trade with labour and environmental standards.

Tax contract
- Transparent, fair, and honest taxation: explain spending; price every promise; cut waste; raise thresholds by £200; new 50% rate above £100,000; add 5p per cigarette pack to fund free checks; around 70% of adults pay lower or unchanged income tax; most others only slightly higher.
